ranked_candidates.text_excerpt: How SQM Turned a 678 km² Mine into an Autonomous Inspection Zone | FlytBase | FlytBase Skip to main content Back to stories Case study How SQM achieved 4× iodine yield improvement by reducing inspections from weeks to hours Download Case Study Mining Industry 0× higher iodine concentration 0% less hazardous terrain exposure TL;DR SQM, a global leader in lithium, iodine, and nitrate production, partnered with Adentu and FlytBase to bring autonomy from concept to daily routine across its 678 km² mining operation in northern Chile. What began as a pilot for detecting irrigation leaks and leaching inefficiencies evolved into a fully automated inspection ecosystem. By connecting DJI Dock-based drones to FlytBase’s autonomy platform and Azure’s analytics engine, SQM cut inspection time from days to hours, achieved more than 95 percent mission reliability, doubled inspection frequency, and improved iodine extraction yield by two percent, all while building internal trust that autonomy could deliver real operational value. Download Case Study In the Atacama Desert, SQM runs one of the largest open-area mining operations on the planet. Every irrigation line, every sprinkler, and every degree of thermal variation can affect extraction performance. Yet until recently, those checks were manual, with field engineers walking or driving kilometers each day, scanning for leaks and disconnected sprinklers. The innovation team wanted to move faster. They needed inspections that did not depend on human endurance or availability. They wanted data that could tell them, every morning, exactly where to act. That need led them to Adentu, a Chile-based integrator specializing in drone autonomy, and FlytBase, the enterprise autonomy platform built for unattended, data-driven drone operations. Together, they set out to answer a question that still challenges most industrial operations: how do you turn autonomy from a proof of concept into an everyday workflow 02 The challenge For years, SQM’s inspection process was limited by scale. Walking inspections meant hours under the desert sun, while driving offered little precision and no thermal context. Problems often went unnoticed for days. "

case_study_discovery.selection_method: Live FlytBase case-study index links scored against lead context; no fixed URL.

sequence.purpose: Acknowledge the operational pain and book discovery
sequence.subject: Atacama inspections: reducing crew exposure across three sites
sequence.body:
Hi Rodrigo,

Thanks for reaching out. Your note about continuous inspections across three Atacama lithium sites—and the cost and exposure associated with contracted crews—sounds like a useful problem to quantify before your Q3 budget discussion.

FlytBase supports autonomous drone operations; the right first step is to understand the inspection workflow rather than assume a particular deployment. Could we schedule 25 minutes to cover the assets inspected, current inspection frequency/cost, hazardous access points, and what a successful pilot would need to prove?

Would early next week work?

Best,
FlytBase Inbound Team
sequence.progression_logic: Lead is high-fit and has a stated budget discussion; respond quickly and ask for a discovery call, not a premature demo.

sequence.timing: After 3 business days if no reply
sequence.purpose: Offer a relevant peer example and clarify the referral
sequence.subject: A mining deployment worth comparing with your Atacama use case
sequence.body:
Hi Rodrigo,

I wanted to share a relevant mining example from FlytBase's public case-study library: How SQM Turned a 678 km² Mine into an Autonomous Inspection Zone | FlytBase | FlytBase. The useful comparison is how autonomous drone operations can reduce repeated travel and keep people away from difficult areas; the actual fit for SQM would depend on your inspection targets, connectivity and site rules.

You mentioned Anglo American referred you. If appropriate, could you share the team or contact who made the introduction? That would help us understand which workflow is most relevant without assuming the two operations are identical.

Would a short working session be useful?

Best,
FlytBase Inbound Team
sequence.progression_logic: Adds proof relevant to mining and asks about referral context while avoiding unsupported performance promises.

sequence.timing: After 5 further business days if no reply
sequence.purpose: Help prepare a budget-ready business case
sequence.subject: Useful inputs for your Q3 inspection business case
sequence.body:
Hi Rodrigo,

To make an initial business case useful for your Q3 discussion, we could model a small set of inputs: annual contracted inspection spend, crew hours in hazardous areas, inspection frequency today versus target, and the cost of a docked-drone pilot at one representative site.

We would also want to confirm who owns operations, HSE, IT/security and budget approval, plus any Chilean aviation or site constraints that need to be considered. If timing has changed, just let me know and I can adjust.

Should I send a one-page discovery checklist, or would you prefer a 20-minute call?

Best,
FlytBase Inbound Team
